name: Akan
overview: Akan was a male Edomite, identified specifically as the son of Ezer. His mention in Scripture is brief, with no additional notes or significant narrative details provided. As an Edomite, he belonged to the descendants of Esau, reflecting the genealogical records important for understanding Israel's neighboring peoples.
namesAndTitles: The individual is known by the name Akan, with an alternate form Jaakan appearing in Scripture. Neither name has a recorded meaning or divine origin in the biblical text, indicating they are proper names without explicit theological significance.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly identifies Akan as the son of Ezer, establishing his immediate paternal lineage. Beyond this, no further family relationships are recorded in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Akan's significance lies primarily in his place within the genealogical record of the Edomites, contributing to the biblical understanding of the descendants of Esau and the broader context of Israel's neighbors. His mention serves to preserve the lineage and tribal affiliations important for historical and theological study, though no direct narrative role or spiritual significance is attributed to him.
